references.text: Describes how the priest is to bring the blood of the sin offering into the tent of meeting and sprinkle it before the curtain in the holy place.

States that the remainder of the sin offering bull is to be burned outside the camp, which aligns with the instruction that a sin offering whose blood is brought into the holy place must not be eaten.
Confirms that the sin offering for the congregation is to be burned outside the camp in the same way as the priest's sin offering.
Moses explains that because the blood was not brought into the holy place, the meat should have been eaten in a holy place.
On the Day of Atonement, the sin offering animals whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place are to be burned outside the camp.
The book of Hebrews refers to this practice and compares it with Jesus' suffering outside the city gate to sanctify the people by his own blood.
